correctness.rationale: The Gram eigenvalues are 1±2t and two copies of 1, so the row basis is legitimate. Independently, with G=I+L+Lᵀ ordered by the sweep and L strictly lower triangular, old and new coefficients a,b obey (I+2L)b=−(I+2Lᵀ)a, since the update in row i uses already updated coefficients for earlier rows and old coefficients for later rows. Thus the characteristic determinant is det[(z+1)I+2zL+2Lᵀ]. In its expansion the identity and four single edge swaps contribute (z+1)^4−16t²z(z+1)². The two disjoint-matchings terms contribute +32t⁴z², and the two full cycle terms give −16t⁴(z+z³) if the order runs along the cycle, or −32t⁴z² otherwise. The former occurs exactly for the four starting vertices and two directions. Taking z+z⁻¹=2c yields the stated cosines; c_other−c_+=4t²(1−t²−t√(2+t²))>0 exactly in the specified positive domain by squaring. c_+ is increasing and c_+(1/2)=1; endpoint derivatives 32/3 and 8 give the square-root gap ratio 2/√3. Normality gives the uniform averaging bound, not pointwise optimality of the finite average. Reversal and cyclic shift exhaust the three-factor case up to inverse and similarity, establishing minimality.
